problemStatement: WR-009 can render one complete Telegram Markdown summary, but a later publisher needs deterministic semantic messages instead of character slicing. Without a rendered-section splitter, message-size handling could cut Markdown fences or company cards and could accidentally reinterpret upstream Weekly Radar facts.

riskAssessment.reason: The splitter must parse rendered Markdown without treating headings inside fenced code as sections, preserve complete top-level sections and company-card bodies, and remain independent of domain calculations and Telegram infrastructure.
riskAssessment.reviewNotes: The input is the explicit rendered Markdown emitted by WR-009. A top-level section is the atomic unit; if one section is larger than caller limits, the splitter returns a typed error instead of attempting unsafe card/body parsing or truncation.

acceptance: A provider-agnostic SemanticMessageSplitter consumes one already-rendered Markdown string and emits typed semantic chunks labeled Executive Summary, Important Transition, Top5, Rising/Dropped, or System Health in source order.
Only explicit top-level rendered sections are recognized; headings inside fenced Markdown code blocks are retained as content, and unclosed fences or unknown top-level sections return typed errors.

Chunks are assembled only from complete rendered sections under caller-supplied character and line limits. Markdown, fenced code blocks, nested Markdown, and company-card content are never truncated or split; an oversized atomic section returns a typed error and no partial result.
The splitter preserves source section text and order without calculating or changing Stage, Ranking, Distance, Top5, Rising, Dropped, System Health, or No Change facts.

Module-local, same-stem companion, and public integration tests cover all five semantic boundaries, WR-009 section aliases, code-fence protection, card/Markdown atomicity, limit packing, invalid input, and provider isolation without changing shared coverage or architecture tests.

The WR-011 spec, implementation plan, reference-impact evidence, active Summary, strict AI Cockpit Finish, archive bundle, and local commit record the delivered boundary, verification, user authorization, remaining non-goals, and local-only next action.

intent.problem: WR-009 produces complete explicit Markdown, while Telegram delivery may need several semantically meaningful messages. Arbitrary character slicing would damage Markdown and lose company-card context.
constraints: Consume only already-rendered explicit sections; do not re-render, parse domain facts, or recalculate Stage, Ranking, Distance, Top5, Rising, Dropped, System Health, or No Change.

Use top-level rendered sections outside fenced code blocks as atomic units. Preserve Markdown, code fences, nested content, and company cards; return typed errors for oversized atomic sections instead of truncating.

Keep the splitter provider-agnostic in the Weekly Radar interface layer. Do not implement network, delivery, retry, receipt, scheduling, persistence, runtime configuration, or external provider integration.
Complete Contract, spec/plan, TDD, focused/module-local/integration verification, strict AI Finish, archive, and local commit. Do not push, open a PR, merge, close, or delete the remote branch.
intent.rationale: A source-preserving section splitter provides a deterministic handoff for a later Publisher while keeping formatting and domain judgment in their existing Work Items. Section-level atomicity is the smallest safe boundary that guarantees Markdown and company-card integrity.
